requirements.reason: Host GPIO, SysTick, and UART logs are implemented and updated.
The 168 MHz clock, reload value of 168000, and tick increments are consistent.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.

Baud-rate handling and the receive-state/queue path exist, but PB6/PB7, 8N1, and NVIC 0/0 specified by R:24 lack complete configuration code or observable configuration state. Low-level configuration may be stubbed; the gap is that the required parameters are not expressed.
PA1-4 have binary outputs and no PWM behavior, but the push-pull, pull-up, and 25 MHz parameters required by R:25 are not expressed. Actual physical pin driving is not required on the host.
Host LED states for PD12-15 are stored and updated by index. D:35-36 permits observable arrays as hardware-effect equivalents; absence of physical BSRRL/BSRRH registers alone is not a defect.
Bit 0 is active-high and initially low; a low level releases the button immediately.

Accelerometer initialization and three-axis reading exist, but the LIS3DSH SPI1/2G/50Hz settings or TM initialization call required by R:28 are not expressed. Low-level configuration may be stubbed; the missing evidence concerns parameters or call paths, not physical hardware.

A raw-temperature input and conversion model exist, but the 12-bit, continuous, divide-by-8, and 144-cycle settings in R:29 are not fully expressed. Configuration stubs are permitted; read functions or comments do not substitute for these parameters.

Simulated ready/value injection and reading exist, but AHB2 clock enabling in R:30 has no call or observable configuration state. DRDY data flow is assessed under host semantics without requiring physical RNG registers.
The call order exactly matches the startup contract.
The exact text, including CRLF, is sent after USART initialization.
The core clock is updated before configuration is called with clock/1000.
Configuration has a nonzero-error branch, and the caller enters an infinite loop.

Initialization preserves PA0-low/released semantics, but GPIOA clock enabling and input-mode configuration in R:44 have no call or state representation. Configuration calls may use empty stubs; the missing call path remains uncovered.
The enumeration values 0, 1, and 2 are correct.
The left-side 10/01/00 mapping and invalid-input default of 00 are correct.
The right-side 10/01/00 mapping and invalid-input default of 00 are correct.
The speed parameter is retained but unused; there is no PWM.
Forward on both sides produces 1010.
Reverse on both sides produces 0101.
Left stopped and right forward produces 0010.
Left forward and right stopped produces 1000.
Left stopped and right reverse produces 0001.
Left reverse and right stopped produces 0100.
Left forward and right reverse produces 1001.
Left reverse and right forward produces 0110.
STOP on both sides clears all four outputs.

The four observable host outputs are initialized low, but the clock and electrical configuration required by R:72-74 are not expressed. The gap is missing evidence of the specified settings or initialization path, not missing physical hardware.
Final states of normal commands use only 10, 01, and 00.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The nine IDs correspond to the nine functions in the required order.
IDs 0-8 directly invoke the lookup-table function, without framing or ACK.
Invalid input is rejected before callme is written. The main loop checks available bytes first and makes no call when empty.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Indices 0-3 return the corresponding bit value; other indices return -1.
The tick increments; a high level must accumulate 250 counts before the state becomes pressed.
A low level immediately clears the counter and releases the button.
Only state comparison, switch/break, and laststate updates are present.
The roll formula is correct when both pointers are valid.
The pitch formula is correct when both pointers are valid.

Host outputs PD12-15 start low, but GPIOD clock enabling and push-pull configuration required by R:118-119 have no call or state representation. Low-level configuration stubs are allowed; configuration cannot be inferred from an initialization function's name.
A valid index sets GPIOD_output[12+i] to 1, which is the required host equivalent of setting the LED. A physical BSRRL write is not required on the host.
A valid index clears GPIOD_output[12+i], preserving observable LED-off semantics. Absence of a physical BSRRH write is not a missing host-model behavior.
Out-of-range and negative indices return immediately without writing other bits.
Continuous UART reading and dispatch are complete, but the one-second condition and t_prev update are replaced by comments.

Initialization returns success as 0, but no actual call evidence supports the TM initialization and 2G/50Hz parameters specified by R:134-135. These cannot be inferred from a function name or success constant. The low-level host implementation of the call may be an empty stub.
Three milli-g values are stored and converted independently using floating-point division by 1000.

A temperature-initialization entry exists, but ADC mode, division, internal channel, and the 144-cycle parameter in R:145-147 are not fully encoded. Permission to stub configuration in D does not permit assuming unspecified parameters.
The code reads software raw data directly, without the start -> EOC -> conversion-value sequence.
The required temperature formula is evaluated in floating point.

An RNG-initialization entry exists, but the R:160-161 sequence of enabling AHB2 before enabling RNG is not expressed. Empty low-level configuration stubs are acceptable; the two missing calls cannot be assumed.

The host checks ready and can return without deadlock, but not-ready returns the valid random value 0 without a separate error state. Not-ready therefore cannot be distinguished from a successful zero. The defect is loss of error-state information, not absence of physical RNG access.
When ready, the original 32-bit value is returned without filtering valid zero or all-ones values.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The first NULL slot receives the callback and the interval converted from seconds to milliseconds; both counters are cleared.
When all 25 slots are occupied, traversal ends without overwriting tasks.
All due tasks execute in slot order; current tick and call count are recorded after each callback.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Each nonempty slot prints its slot number and numcalls.
There is no removal, priority, or preemption; NULL slots are skipped.
baud=0 selects 9600 and emits an fprintf warning.

UART initialization and receive state exist, but the PB6/PB7 alternate function, 100 MHz, push-pull/pull-up, 8N1, bidirectional/no-flow-control, and NVIC parameters in R:193-196 are not fully expressed. The stubs need not access physical peripherals.

The 200-byte receive buffer and RXNE data path exist, but the USART-enable call/state required by R:195 is not expressed. An empty low-level USART_Cmd stub is allowed; an absent enable operation cannot be credited as complete.
RXNE reads DR and enqueues the byte. A full buffer rejects the new byte; unrelated interrupts have no effect.

Characters are appended in order to the host TX log, but the per-byte readiness wait required by R:202-204 and D:63-64 is not simulated. The gap is the state condition, not absence of physical USART_SendData.
The ring-buffer read is delegated; an empty buffer returns 0.
The char conversion is retained, matching the specified signed-char interpretation.
The counter difference is returned.
All five required fields are present.
An already-enabled buffer reports an error and is skipped. Normal allocation uses calloc to zero memory and initializes the fields.
A valid nonfull buffer writes at n_w modulo size and increments n_w; a full buffer is not overwritten.
A nonempty buffer reads at n_r modulo size and increments n_r; an empty buffer returns 0.
n_r and n_w are compared directly.
Occupancy >= size replaces the specified nonempty-and-equal-modulo-indices rule. They agree for a normal full queue but may differ for public states such as occupancy exceeding size after resizing.
Returns n_w-n_r.
realloc uses a temporary pointer; failure preserves the old allocation and success updates size.
The buffer is cleared and freed, fields are cleared, and enabled is reset; NULL returns false.
Only contents are cleared; read/write counters and configuration are unchanged.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Adding 1 to uint32_t provides 32-bit wraparound.

func1 passes the same argument to func2 and returns its result. D:72 explicitly allows an equivalent host C implementation; downgrading it for not delivering ARM LR instructions exceeds this task's scope.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Constants are public; START/STOP do not introduce a framing protocol.
Only 0/1 is written to the designated array positions, making all outputs observable.
Only bit 0 is modified.
Three-axis raw-data injection and reading share the same variables.
Injected raw data enters the same formula path.
ready/value are injected together and do not deadlock, but a not-ready return of 0 is indistinguishable from a valid random zero, leaving not-ready observability incomplete.
DR/RXNE injection invokes the same interrupt handler.
Characters are appended to the TX log while maintaining its length and terminator; appending stops at capacity.
Production single-step UART/button/task entries are provided without main. Missing timing logic is scored separately under R046.

A generic buffer-deletion function exists, but UART's msg is a private static object with a heap allocation. No reachable code path frees that instance, and external code cannot obtain its address. R:299's requirement that all allocations be releasable is not fully covered.
Null pointers, invalid indices, and full buffers have safe returns.
Unused speed/no PWM, no task removal, and the raw-byte protocol are preserved.

metric: coverage of 88 statically reviewable requirement leaves; 7 preclassified leaves unassessed
note: All 650 lines of discobot.c and the 128-line header were read. Hardware-configuration comments in the host model were not treated as implemented behavior.
scope_review_policy: R+D host-equivalent task contract; supplied A constrains shared-API methods; configuration stubs allowed, missing required values/paths not invented; Direct not penalized by unsupplied A; no candidate changes
scope_review_notes: R:1–16 and D:7–12 define project-level host-equivalent scope, not reconstruction of real upstream firmware.
D:11–12/A:273–276 allow configuration stubs; this does not waive R-specified configuration values/order.
D:72 allows transparent C semantics for host assembly functionality.
R:299 allocation-release obligation remains applicable regardless of hardware stub permissions.
Original standalone serializers record preliminary decisions; active JSON after this scope reconciliation is authoritative.

review_lineage.reason: Correct task scope interpretation consistently after reading R+D+A; preserve actual functional failures; not score selection.

changes.old_reason: The host returns safely when not ready, but the target's no-timeout DRDY wait exists only in a comment, without an actual implementation path.
changes.new_reason: The host checks ready and can return without deadlock, but not-ready returns the valid random value 0 without a separate error state. Not-ready therefore cannot be distinguished from a successful zero. The defect is loss of error-state information, not absence of physical RNG access.
